subject: Clarifying non-training carve-outs and EEA transfer pathway — DPA next steps

Subject: DPA — explicit non-training language + EEA transfer question

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the call earlier. Medixa needs the DPA to explicitly confirm that customer-provided PHI and other Medixa-controlled data will not be used to train or improve models accessible outside our tenancy. Specifically we need:

- A clear definition of “Training”/“Model Improvement” that excludes internal performance telemetry but prohibits using any customer data for model updates that could influence downstream model weights or public model releases.
- A commitment that any telemetry used for service quality will be pseudonymized and cannot be reverse-engineered into proprietary data.
- An affirmation that cross-border transfers from the EEA will follow standard SCCs or equivalent safeguards, and a notes section describing where data may be processed (US infra for hosted evaluation routes).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a one-paragraph carve-out that says: "Customer Data will not be used to train or improve foundation models or shared model weights; limited operational telemetry for performance and reliability (e.g., aggregate latency metrics) may be used in pseudonymized form for internal service improvements only."

Also attach the redlines we received from procurement — I put them in the PDF. We need to close this by end of week to keep the go-live cadence.

Best,
Alice
Alice Johnson
Head of Platform Integrations
Medixa Health

Marissa / Alice —

Below is a legal-friendly redline that balances Medixa’s ask and our operational needs. Happy to tweak language further but this is the form we can commit to in a Hosted + Dedicated configuration: 

--- PROPOSED CLAUSE (to insert into DPA) ---
"Customer Data" means any data, content, or information provided by Customer to Redwood under the Agreement.

"Model Training and Weight Updates" means the use of customer data for the purpose of adjusting, re-training, fine-tuning, or otherwise changing the parameters, weights, or topology of a machine learning model such that those changes persist beyond ephemeral inference-time caches.

Non-Training Commitment: Except as expressly permitted below, Redwood will not use Customer Data to perform Model Training and Weight Updates for any foundation or shared models accessible outside Customer’s dedicated environment.

Permitted Operational Uses: Redwood may process Customer Data for: (i) ephemeral inference-time caching necessary to serve requests; (ii) pseudonymized and aggregated telemetry used exclusively for internal monitoring, performance tuning, and reliability fixes, provided such telemetry cannot be reconstructed to identify Customer or individual data subjects; and (iii) compliance and fraud detection where required by law.

Cross-Border Transfers: Redwood will ensure any transfers from the EEA to the United States are subject to appropriate safeguards (e.g., SCCs) or rely on an approved transfer mechanism and will document subprocessors and transfer locations in its subprocessor list.

---------------------------------------------

If Medixa is comfortable with the wording on the non-training commitment and the permitted operational uses bullet (we avoided absolute bans on ephemeral caching), we can accept signature on this. Rishi — please confirm if this matches what we discussed commercially (discount/commitment tradeoffs) and whether we need to append a clause about SOC2/audit access.

-Neha Kapoor

If legal signs off, I’ll add a short paragraph to the SOW about the retention and a small credit for the compliance work. Priyom / Lauren — please prep the DocuSign envelope and include the redline PDF and the clean DPA. I’ve added the requested SCC callout to the redline.
